thread:
oncall-bot: 🚨 Paging: P99 latency SLO breach detected for /v1/generate-stream (region: us-west-2). Alert id: alert-2134
oncall-bot: p95=220ms, p99=1.9s over 5m, error rate +1%, active tailers: 4
alex: seeing it too. tail spikes coincide with higher batch sizes on cont-batch-worker pool.
priya: any customer reports?
maria: no direct customer tickets yet, but internal synthetic probes show streaming stalls — tokens stop for ~1.5s before catching up.
rob (sre): @alex can you grab the cont-batch metrics? queue depth, batch size distribution, and seqlen histogram pls
alex: pulling now. attaching quick dump: `curl -s http://metrics/api?m=batch.size.dist,contbatch.queue,stream.stalls` -> results show median batch=8, 95pct=64, max=128. Mixed seqlen wide: median seqlen=32, 95=512.
priya: that 95pct batch=64 is suspicious. streaming path shouldn't accumulate >32 normally. Did autoscaler add more workers?
alex: autoscaler added 2 nodes ~10m ago for throughput. config shows `cont_batch.max_batch=128` (default), `fair_share_enabled=true`.
maria: codepath: streaming requests share the same scheduling lane as non-streaming in cont-batch. If large batches form, streaming KV flush/prefetch latency increases.
rob (sre): can we reduce `cont_batch.max_batch` to 32 live and see effect? quick config patch or rollout?
alex: we can patch the config on pool contbatch-usw2. command: ```
#!/bin/bash
rctl update pool contbatch-usw2 --set cont_batch.max_batch=32
```
priya: +1 do it. Do we need a canary? risk: throughput drop for high-throughput customers.
maria: we can canary on 10% of nodes first, but tailers are causing SLO breach, I'd prioritize reducing tail.
oncall-bot: runbook reminder: `cont-batch-tail-latency` mitigation steps: reduce max_batch, enable seqlen-aware batching, isolate streaming lane.
alex: applying canary: `rctl update pool contbatch-usw2 --selector=node-role=canary --set cont_batch.max_batch=32`
deploy-bot: applied configuration to 2 nodes (canary) (change id: cfg-98765)
alex: monitoring.. p95->180ms, p99->950ms on canary nodes after ~60s
priya: good signal. can we also bump `fair_share_weight` for streaming class to 3? default is 1. that should favor small streaming batches in scheduler.
maria: yes `scheduler.fair_share.streaming_weight=3` is safe to roll to canary too.
alex: applied streaming_weight canary. metrics: streaming queue wait time reduced by ~40% on canary.
rob (sre): what's customer impact delta? any 4xx/5xx?
maria: no increase in 5xx. overall request throughput stable. internal probe success rate unchanged.
priya: canary looks healthy. plan: roll config to remaining nodes over 5 minutes, then monitor for throughput drop for high-batch workloads.
alex: rolling to remaining 10 nodes now: `rctl update pool contbatch-usw2 --set cont_batch.max_batch=32,scheduler.fair_share.streaming_weight=3 --rolling 10m`
deploy-bot: started rolling config to 10 nodes (batch size 2 nodes/min)
oncall-bot: note: alert auto-escalation paused for 10m during mitigation window
alex: halfway through roll. p99 across pool moved from 1.9s -> 720ms.
rob (sre): nice. add a temporary KV cache TTL bump? streaming stalls looked like KV miss churn when big batches kicked eviction. We could increase `kv.prefetch_ttl` to 15s from 5s on streaming workers.
maria: do it on streaming lane only. Command: `rctl update pool contbatch-streaming --set kv.prefetch_ttl=15s`
priya: careful, longer TTL increases memory pressure. monitor mem usage.
alex: applied to streaming lane. mem +3% so far.
rob (sre): ok. main metrics show p99 now ~520ms, p95 ~160ms, error rate normalized.
maria: root cause hypothesis: mixed sequence lengths + high max_batch allowed large batches combining short streaming requests with long non-streaming workloads; scheduler fairness didn't sufficiently prioritize streaming -> KV churn + stalls -> tail latency.
priya: post-incident actions: 1) set default cont_batch.max_batch=32 2) implement seqlen-aware batching in scheduler 3) add runbook step to isolate streaming lane under SLO breach 4) add synthetic probe for streaming stall detection 5) revisit autoscaler policy to avoid sudden node additions that increase batch variance
alex: creating follow-up ticket: PROD-8732 "cont-batch: seqlen-aware scheduler + default max_batch change" and linking graphs.
rob (sre): assign to eng-runtime + eng-oncall for followup. add timeline and metric snapshots.
maria: tagging customer-impact: potential latency degradation for a few customers during the initial spike; no confirmed errors. we'll notify CS with a brief note.
priya: i'll draft the customer comms: short summary + what we changed + monitoring link.
oncall-bot: Incident resolved: SLO alerts returned to normal for /v1/generate-stream. Incident window: 2026-03-14T02:11:30Z - 2026-03-14T02:24:35Z
alex: handing off to night oncall @rob. please pick up follow-ups in ticket PROD-8732, and continue monitoring synthetic probes for 6 hours.
rob (sre): ack, taking handoff. I'll leave a checklist in the ticket and set a 1h heartbeat.
maria: thx team. :tada:
priya: good work everyone. I'll post a short blameless summary in #incidents tomorrow.
rob (sre): tagging runbook: `kb/cont-batch-tail-latency` updated with temp knobs we applied.
alex: end of thread
